objective: Design an independently maintainable release-management business module for project-scoped release windows, version applications, workflow-linked approval state, baselines, version lineage, and real-time reports without placing business state inside platform modules.
users: Project developer registering and tracking a version application
Tester and configured approver reviewing a release application
Configuration manager maintaining windows and baseline records
Platform administrator maintaining permissions without substituting for business approval

requirements.statement: The planned ccb-release module must own release windows, applications, baselines, reports, and their business state.
acceptance: No release business table or release state machine is implemented in system or workflow modules
The module can be tested with external port stubs
requirements.source: User selected architecture option A and required platform design to remain separate
counterexample: Release application status is inferred only from Flowable tables
Release tables are placed in platform/system

requirements.statement: Every protected operation must enforce tenant, current project, RBAC, data scope, and entity authorization on the server.
acceptance: Cross-project and unauthorized requests are rejected
List, detail, attachment, report, and export use the same project scope
requirements.source: Confirmed role and project-context rules plus repository governance
counterexample: Frontend visibility is the only authorization
Client-supplied actor identity is trusted

requirements.statement: Release windows must enforce immutable project and code, ordered dates, same-year production dates, no overlap in one project, auditable edits, and a regular-submission switch.
acceptance: Invalid order, cross-year production, and overlapping windows cannot be saved
Every allowed edit records reason and before/after values
After regular baseline succeeds, the regular-submission switch is permanently locked off
counterexample: A window project can be changed
A window can be disabled or deleted

requirements.statement: The module must derive regular, additional, overdue, overdue-additional, or emergency scenarios from project, dates, switch state, and history and map them to five fixed workflow codes.
acceptance: All date boundaries and additional combinations yield one deterministic scenario
The applicant cannot select a workflow definition
counterexample: A regular application can be submitted on or after production start
The user manually chooses regular or emergency type

requirements.statement: An application must contain one physical subsystem and at least one unique delivery unit with a fixed artifact type snapshot and a nonblank version without spaces.
acceptance: Even a draft rejects missing delivery units or versions
One delivery unit cannot be repeated in an application
counterexample: An empty application draft is saved
Artifact type is editable in the application

requirements.statement: Requirements, overdue reason, additional reason, emergency explanation, and optional attachments must follow scenario-specific validation.
acceptance: Regular submission requires at least one requirement number
Emergency submission requires the emergency explanation but not a requirement number
Attachments are optional in every scenario
counterexample: Emergency attachment is mandatory
Requirements are stored as comma-separated text

requirements.statement: Duplicate, in-flight, additional, emergency, and cross-window history checks must follow the confirmed blocking and warning rules.
acceptance: Conflict results identify delivery unit, old and new version, application number, and required action
Any additional delivery unit upgrades the whole regular application scenario
counterexample: Emergency history automatically becomes an additional scenario
History in another window blocks submission

requirements.statement: Draft, review, return, withdrawal, approval, baseline, and cancellation transitions must preserve immutable submission rounds and operation history.
acceptance: Illegal state transitions are rejected
An in-review application must be withdrawn before it can be canceled or edited
Every cancellation requires a reason
Resubmission creates a new workflow round and retains previous opinions and signatures
Crossing production start requires explicit emergency conversion
counterexample: An approved application can be edited or withdrawn
Resubmission overwrites the prior workflow instance

requirements.statement: The module must integrate approval through five fixed workflow codes and consume workflow lifecycle results without reading workflow private tables.
acceptance: Missing or invalid published workflow blocks submission but not draft save
Testing review precedes configuration-management review
Each approval round produces only a whole-application pass or fail result
counterexample: The module queries wf_task directly
One delivery unit passes while another fails in the same application

requirements.statement: Business detail, workflow progress, opinions, rounds, and signature data must describe the same application and task as the unified inbox and done list.
acceptance: The application detail shows current node, assignee, progress, round history, opinions, and returned signature data
Unified task navigation and business detail resolve the same application and workflow task
requirements.source: User-confirmed workflow progress and unified-task behavior
counterexample: Workflow progress is visible only in the generic workflow page
A second business approval ledger replaces workflow task history

requirements.statement: Regular applications must enter one irreversible window-level baseline batch only after the production end date and after all noncancelled regular applications are approved.
acceptance: Blocking applications produce zero baseline writes and a complete blocker list
Successful baseline closes and permanently locks regular submission and cannot be repeated
counterexample: Each regular application exposes its own baseline button
A window baseline runs on the production end date

requirements.statement: Emergency applications must record approval and then be automatically and idempotently added to a per-application baseline batch.
acceptance: Success creates exactly one emergency batch
Failure retains approved status and can retry without duplicate records
counterexample: An emergency application requires a manual application-level baseline confirmation
Retry creates another baseline batch

requirements.statement: Baseline details and current pointers must preserve physical-subsystem and delivery-unit version lineage without deleting replaced versions.
acceptance: Batch plus physical subsystem plus delivery unit uniquely identifies a detail
A later emergency version remains current when an older regular window is subsequently baselined
counterexample: Version string ordering determines current baseline
Replacing a baseline deletes the prior version

requirements.statement: Additional and emergency versions must form an explicit, queryable replacement chain at delivery-unit granularity.
acceptance: Every replaced line identifies its replacing application, version, and effective date
Only the endpoint of an additional regular chain enters the regular batch
counterexample: A replaced version is physically deleted
All intermediate additional versions enter the regular baseline batch

requirements.statement: Application actions, window edits, attachments, exports, workflow rounds, and baseline changes must be fully auditable.
acceptance: Audit data identifies actor, object, timestamp, reason, and structured before/after values where applicable
Cancellation is impossible without a recorded reason
requirements.source: User-confirmed edit, cancellation, and traceability rules
counterexample: A window change overwrites data without its prior value
A canceled application has no reason or actor

requirements.statement: Project and window reports must aggregate current business data in real time with confirmed deduplication, drill-down, and Excel export rules.
acceptance: Project and single-window totals match their filtered detail data
Exported sheets match UI filters and permissions
No approval-efficiency metric is emitted
counterexample: Draft and canceled records inflate business-scale metrics
Attachments are included in the export archive

requirements.statement: The business module must depend only on declared project-context, master-data, workflow, notification, and attachment ports whose platform implementations are designed separately.
acceptance: Current module design contains no platform table or internal implementation
Platform capability work is tracked as a separate design dependency
requirements.source: User explicitly required platform design to be separated
counterexample: This module design adds fields to wf_definition
Release code writes sys_notification or MinIO keys directly

requirements.statement: The implementation Agent must initialize form metadata, menu permissions, fixed workflow-code mocks, master-data mocks, applications, baselines, reports, and notifications idempotently for local development.
acceptance: A fresh local database displays the complete module without manual setup
Repeated startup does not duplicate initialization records
requirements.source: RDDMP metadata and mock contracts plus user-confirmed mock requirement
counterexample: Developers must configure fields or workflows manually after first startup
Production silently falls back to local mock providers

requirements.statement: The module must expose desktop list, form, detail, workflow-progress, baseline, and report pages by reusing RDDMP shared UI patterns.
acceptance: A desktop user can complete each core path
Loading, empty, error, forbidden, submitting, readonly, conflict, and long-text states are visible
requirements.source: User confirmed desktop-only scope and page design
counterexample: Workflow progress is available only on the generic workflow page
Mobile acceptance is claimed in this requirement

invariants: One application belongs to one tenant, project, window, and physical subsystem
One delivery unit appears once per application
One regular baseline batch exists per window and one emergency batch per emergency application
Baseline history is never physically deleted
Platform private tables are not accessed by ccb-release
constraints: Java 17, Spring Boot 3.4.4, MySQL 8.4, Vue 3, TypeScript
Desktop-only exception approved for this requirement
Platform capability implementation is outside this design
non_goals: Workflow engine, unified task, notification, signature, and persistent attachment internal implementation
Artifact file storage and semantic version validation

selected_approach.name: Single ccb-release business module with internal domain partitions
selected_approach.reason: Window baseline, application conflict, version lineage, and reporting need cohesive transactions and ownership while remaining outside platform modules.

alternatives.name: Separate Maven modules for windows, applications, and baselines
alternatives.rejected_because: Adds excessive cross-module transaction and event complexity for the current scope.

alternatives.name: Workflow-centered business state
alternatives.rejected_because: Would couple release rules and reports to Flowable and weaken independent business maintenance.

components.name: window
components.responsibility: Own release-window dates, switch, overlap, audit, and regular-baseline readiness

components.name: application
components.responsibility: Own application data, scenarios, conflicts, lifecycle, and submission rounds

components.name: baseline
components.responsibility: Own regular batches, emergency auto-baseline jobs, current pointers, and replacement lineage

components.name: reporting
components.responsibility: Provide project and window real-time aggregates, drill-down filters, and Excel exports

components.name: release-ui
components.responsibility: Provide desktop windows, applications, workflow context, baselines, and reports

interfaces.name: ReleaseProjectContextPort
interfaces.contract: Return authenticated current project and authorize project access.

interfaces.name: ReleaseMasterDataPort
interfaces.contract: Query physical subsystems, delivery units, artifact types, and display snapshots.

interfaces.name: ReleaseWorkflowPort
interfaces.contract: Resolve and start a published workflow by fixed code, terminate it, query progress, and deliver lifecycle events.

interfaces.name: ReleaseAttachmentPort
interfaces.contract: Upload, authorize, preview, download, and delete persistent business attachments.

data_flows.input: Current project, business date, master-data selection, and application fields

transitions: update current pointers and application results

error_handling.behavior: Existing snapshots remain readable; new selection or protected writes fail clearly.
error_handling.recovery: Restore the adapter and retry without losing form state.

error_handling.condition: Workflow missing, unpublished, invalid, or unavailable
error_handling.behavior: Draft save remains available but submission does not change application state.
error_handling.recovery: Publish or restore the fixed-code workflow and resubmit.

error_handling.behavior: Reject stale rowVersion and preserve the newer server state.
error_handling.recovery: Refresh and retry an allowed action.

error_handling.behavior: Create no batch and return the complete blocker list.
error_handling.recovery: Approve or cancel blockers and retry after the allowed date.

error_handling.behavior: Keep approved status and record an idempotent failed job.
Keep the committed business result and record a pending notification event.

security: no trusted actor fields from clients
no credentials or object keys in business logs
compatibility: display numbering decoupled from internal IDs
existing platform modules unchanged by this design
operations: idempotent workflow events and baseline jobs
fresh and repeatable local mock initialization
read-only preservation of business evidence on rollback

verification_strategy.signal: Release business ownership remains inside ccb-release and every protected path enforces tenant, project, RBAC, data-scope, and entity authorization.
verification_strategy.method: Architecture dependency checks plus service and API authorization tests.

verification_strategy.signal: Window, scenario, validation, conflict, and state-transition tests cover normal and boundary cases.
Workflow and other platform interactions pass consumer-port contract tests without private table access, and business detail matches unified tasks.
verification_strategy.method: Stub adapters, architecture checks, and integration contract tests.

verification_strategy.signal: Baseline concurrency, retries, lineage, and latest-pointer assertions remain stable under repeated execution.
verification_strategy.method: Transactional integration tests against MySQL-compatible schema.

verification_strategy.signal: Audited changes and operations preserve actor, reason, object, time, and before/after values where applicable.
Report API, drill-down detail, and exported workbook totals match.
verification_strategy.method: Seeded data cross-check and workbook assertions.

verification_strategy.signal: Fresh startup and repeated startup produce the same expected mock and metadata records.
verification_strategy.method: Fresh database and idempotent reload verification.

verification_strategy.signal: Desktop business paths and all asynchronous UI states are usable without console errors.
verification_strategy.method: Frontend build and real desktop browser acceptance.

assumptions.text: The platform will later provide an authenticated current-project port.
assumptions.basis: User defined the top-level project as the working context.
assumptions.falsifier: Platform design chooses no server-verifiable project context.

assumptions.text: R&D management will provide physical-subsystem and delivery-unit query data.
assumptions.basis: User assigned master-data ownership to R&D management.
assumptions.falsifier: R&D management cannot expose a stable adapter contract.

assumptions.text: Workflow can resolve the current published version by stable code and emit lifecycle events.
assumptions.basis: User selected workflow-code integration and unified tasks.
assumptions.falsifier: Platform workflow design cannot safely expose these operations.

assumptions.text: Persistent attachment IDs and preview will be provided by a later platform design.
assumptions.basis: Current file-preview capability is temporary and user requires application attachments.

unknowns.question: What are the final display formats for application numbers and baseline batch numbers?
unknowns.impact: Only display and configuration; internal identity and relationships are unaffected.

unknowns.question: How will each platform port be implemented internally?
unknowns.impact: Blocks integrated implementation but is intentionally handled by a separate approved platform design.

unknowns.question: What exact DTOs will future project and R&D modules publish?
unknowns.impact: Adapter DTO mapping may change while consumer semantics remain stable.

decisions.decision: Use one ccb-release business module with internal domain partitions.
Separate platform capability design from this module design.
decisions.reason: Keep business and platform ownership independently reviewable.

decisions.decision: Use five fixed workflow codes rather than a workflow-scene binding UI.
decisions.reason: Stable codes are sufficient and avoid duplicate configuration.

decisions.decision: Use window-level regular baseline and automatic per-application emergency baseline.
decisions.reason: Matches production-window governance and emergency replacement behavior.

decisions.decision: Deliver desktop UI only in this requirement.

risks.risk: Platform ports are not ready when module implementation begins.
risks.mitigation: Approve a separate platform design first and use contract stubs only for local module work.

risks.risk: Concurrent additional and emergency baselines corrupt the current pointer.
risks.mitigation: Use unique constraints, locking, explicit lineage, idempotency, and concurrency tests.

risks.risk: Real-time reports degrade as data grows.
risks.mitigation: Scope queries, index dimensions, observe query plans, and add summaries only from measured need.

risks.risk: Desktop-only pages are unusable on phones.
risks.impact: Mobile users cannot complete the flow.
risks.mitigation: Record the approved exception and deliver mobile adaptation as a separate requirement.

approval.evidence: User approved the conversational module design and authorized document creation; landed revision still requires review.
